section_summary: This section contains industrial licensing agreements involving Japanese firms and foreign manufacturers, covering carburetors, diesel engines, aircraft propellers, mineral processing, boilers, and shipboard equipment. The agreements set out territorial rights, technical assistance, royalties, patent rights, and termination terms. A separate report records royalties paid and unpaid under the mineral-processing agreement.

subfiles.title: Claudel–Mitsubishi carburetor license agreement
subfiles.from: Société Anonyme des Carburateurs et Appareils Claudel
subfiles.about: Claudel grants Mitsubishi Japanese and Manchurian manufacturing rights for aviation carburetors.
subfiles.summary: The French agreement lists licensed carburetor types and patents, drawings to be supplied, a 250,000-franc fee, and a 10 percent royalty after the first 1,500 units. It also covers technical staff, improvements, exclusivity, renewal, and arbitration.

subfiles.title: Mitsui–Burmeister & Wain diesel-engine license agreement
subfiles.about: Burmeister & Wain licenses Mitsui to manufacture and sell several types of diesel engines in Japanese-controlled territories.
subfiles.summary: The license covers marine and stationary diesel engines, patent use, drawings, technical training, and promotion. It specifies horsepower-based royalties and payment currencies, delegates manufacture to Mitsui's affiliated Tamano shipyard, and provides for termination and Copenhagen arbitration. It replaces a 1928 agreement.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Mitsui–Burmeister & Wain agreement
subfiles.from: Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, Ltd. and Burmeister & Wain
subfiles.about: The parties coordinate Mitsui's diesel-engine agency duties with the license agreement.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui agrees to promote Burmeister & Wain engines and limits when it may deal in other makers' engines. The supplement defines related royalty obligations and replaces a 1928 supplement. Burmeister & Wain's representative signed in Tokyo on October 8, 1941.

subfiles.title: Amendment to Mitsui aircraft-propeller license
subfiles.about: United Aircraft and Mitsui amend their 1934 propeller license to address aircraft, engines, and replacement parts crossing licensed territories.
subfiles.summary: The amendment defines United's affiliated companies and revises shipment and sale rights for aircraft, engines, licensed propellers, and replacement parts entering or leaving Mitsui's territory. Its effect in other exclusive licensees' territories depends on corresponding amendments or termination of their licenses.

subfiles.title: Hamilton Standard–Mitsui aircraft-propeller license
subfiles.about: Hamilton Standard grants Mitsui a ten-year license to manufacture light-metal controllable-pitch propellers in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The agreement defines products and territory, permits specified cross-border movement with aircraft and engines, and provides design data, manufacturing guidance, and training. It sets a $45,000 initial fee and further payments for improvements, subject to U.S. export approval. It also governs confidentiality, marking, termination, arbitration, and the return of technical materials.

subfiles.title: Consolidated Mining and Smelting–Mitsui Mining sulphide-roasting agreement
subfiles.from: The Consolidated Mining and Smelting Company of Canada, Limited
subfiles.about: The Canadian company supplies Mitsui Mining with a mineral-sulphide roasting process for use in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The agreement provides engineering data and a trial of the roasting process, followed by tonnage-based royalties if Mitsui adopts it. It limits use to Mitsui's plants, requires exchange of improvements and operating records, and sets reporting, audit, default, and transfer provisions.

subfiles.title: Report on Mitsui Mining's foreign patent contract
subfiles.about: The report accounts for royalties paid and unpaid under a foreign-owned patent contract.
subfiles.summary: It lists payments made through Japan's enemy-property custodian and unpaid royalties for 1942–1946, citing wartime foreign-exchange and industrial-property controls.

subfiles.title: James Howden–Mitsui boiler and air-heater agreement, with cover and patent schedules
subfiles.about: James Howden licenses Mitsui to manufacture ship boilers and air heaters at its Japanese works.
subfiles.summary: The nonexclusive agreement covers specified Scotch boilers and turbulent-flow air heaters, with a sterling license fee and royalties based on heating surface. It provides drawings and technical particulars, records and inspection rights, exchange of improvements, patent protections, and a fifteen-year term. The parties signed in London and Glasgow in February 1936; patent schedules follow.

subfiles.title: Shipboard turbo-compressor patent license
subfiles.about: An indenture licenses manufacture and installation of patented turbo-compressors and related shipboard appliances in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages describe a £5,000 payment, nonexclusive rights limited to installation on ships in Japan, restrictions on assignment and sublicensing, and a term tied to the patents. They also address technical drawings, assistance, quality, notice of installations, and a horsepower-based charge. The document continues beyond page 340.
